data.title: AI can do boring work, decisions must belong to judges: Ex-CJI Chandrachud
data.description:
Former Chief Justice of India D Y Chandrachud on Saturday said artificial intelligence can help courts with dull and routine tasks but stressed that the decision and the reasons for it must remain the responsibility of the judge.

Speaking at an event on 'AI for all: AI governance and trust, the case for judicial access and an empowered India', he said a human being must decide and sign every judgment.

"Look at what these (AI) tools have in common: transcription, translation, listing, scrutiny of defects. It is dull work, and it is where a court loses most of its time. The tragedy of the Indian judicial system is that judges spend their time doing work which should least occupy their time, dull and routine work when their work should be really concentrated on real-time decision making," Chandrachud said.

 

"I have come to think that the best use of AI in a court is the boring one. The trouble begins when the technology is asked to do something more interesting," he added.

Referring to instances of AI-generated fake legal citations, Chandrachud cited two Supreme Court cases involving fabricated references to judicial precedents.

In one case, a trial court in Andhra Pradesh relied on four Supreme Court judgments that did not exist. The apex court later held that a decision based on non-existent judgments was not merely an error but misconduct, he said.

In another case, a tribunal's orders cited genuine Supreme Court judgments but included fabricated passages attributed to them, he added.

"A citation of a law report that does not exist can be caught in 30 seconds. A real judgment with an invented paragraph will pass every casual check," Chandrachud said.

"Every citation and every translation produced by a machine must be checked by a human being, and a record must be kept of each use," he added.

The former CJI said the Supreme Court's AI Committee had published draft regulations on the use of artificial intelligence in courts on June 3 this year.

He said the proposed regulations were intended to apply from the Supreme Court to trial courts and tribunals, and were based on the principles of human primacy, transparency, accountability, data protection and judicial independence.

Chandrachud said the draft regulations permitted the use of AI for case management, transcription, translation and research, but prohibited its use for assessing a person's risk for bail or determining the credibility of a witness.

"They (the draft regulations) bar opaque systems wherever rights or liberty are at stake. They propose a register of every AI tool a court uses and a database of incidents when something goes wrong. Parties who use AI in their submissions would have to say so," he said.

Suggesting three areas that required attention before the regulations are finalised, Chandrachud called for a mechanism allowing litigants to challenge AI-related errors, including mistranslations, training for district judges and independent audits.

He also outlined five tests for the use of AI in courts.

"The first test is that a human being decides and signs. A judgment is an exercise of public power by a person who has taken an oath, gives reasons for the decision, and remains accountable through the appellate processes," he said.

"A language model that has taken no oath; it cannot be asked to explain itself in a higher form, and it does not lose sleep over an innocent man in custody. Let it find the papers, translate them, and summarise them. The decision and the reasons for it must belong to the judge," Chandrachud said.

The second test, he said, was that a person's liberty must never be determined by a probability score.

"A bail decision requires the court to consider the individual before it, the allegations, the material on the record, and the circumstances of the case. A risk score may provide certain information based on patterns but it cannot replace an individual assessment. Any use of such technology must therefore remain consistent with the constitutional protection of liberty under Article 21," he said.

The third test was that litigants must be informed when AI has been used in their cases.

"If a tool was used to translate my evidence or summarise my appeal, I should be able to find that out, and I should be able to say that it got something wrong, terribly wrong. That is why I ask you to remember that our translated judgments are vetted by human beings," he said.

"A translation that nobody has checked is a rumour about a judgment," he added.

The fourth test, he said, was that technology should reach people at the end of the queue.

"The strongest case for AI in our courts is the judgment that reaches a litigant in Marathi or Assamese on the day it is delivered, and the next date of hearing that can be asked for by a voice on a basic phone," Chandrachud said.

The fifth test was data security. He advocated a sovereign database and an India-built AI model.

"None of these tests is hostile to technology. Each one describes what a good judge already does," he said.

Chandrachud also underlined the need for technological assistance in the justice system, given the large backlog of cases.

Citing a statement made by the Law Minister in the Rajya Sabha in July this year, he said about 5.64 crore cases were pending across courts in the country.

India had roughly 15 judges per 10 lakh people, against the Law Commission's recommendation of 50 judges per 10 lakh people made in 1987, while a district court judge handled about 2,200 cases on average, he said.

The former CJI also referred to legal aid spending of Rs 6.46 per person annually, according to the India Justice Report.

"That will not buy a cup of tea in most places," he said.

Listing technology initiatives already under way, Chandrachud mentioned the use of AI for transcribing court arguments and the Supreme Court's translation tool Suvas, which has translated judgments into 18 Indian languages.

He also referred to the use of speech-to-text technology to record witness depositions in all trial courts in Kerala since November 1, 2025.

A tool being tested in collaboration with IIT Madras would help identify defects in fresh court filings, he said.

Chandrachud also had a word of advice for the legal profession, saying lawyers must read judgments in full before citing them.

He said, citing the Bar Council of India's position, that advocates could not blame technology for errors in their submissions.

data.title: South states must unite against unfair delimitation: K'taka CM Shivakumar
data.description:
Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar on Saturday said the proposed Delimitation Bill was unfair to southern states, asserting that they would have to collectively raise their concerns to protect their political representation, while also criticising the Centre for not convening an all-party meeting to discuss the issue.

Speaking about his Delhi visit and the delimitation issue, Shivakumar said Karnataka, along with other southern states, would strongly put forward its concerns, adding that the contribution of South India to the country must be recognised.

"Let them do politics. But it is unfair to the southern states. They want to increase the number of seats, and they feel that our southern states will become a minority in the country," he said.

 

He said that the Chief Ministers of Keralam and Telangana would meet on Sunday to discuss the issue and evolve a common position to safeguard the interests of their respective states.

"Tomorrow, all the Chief Ministers are meeting. Satheesan, Revanth Reddy and I are meeting. We will definitely have to put forward our points and protect the interests of our states and South India. South India is giving more strength to the country in every sense. So, they cannot silence our voice. We will speak on that," Shivakumar said.

He also questioned the Centre's approach to the proposed exercise, saying that political parties should have been consulted before moving ahead with the issue.

"We expected them to call an all-party meeting and discuss the issue with our political parties. I think they have not called an all-party meeting. What Siddaramaiah said is also right. They should have called an all-party meeting and discussed it with us," he said.

Asked about Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu's statement on the delimitation issue, Shivakumar declined to comment, saying, "He is an alliance partner, and I definitely don't want to comment on that."

Meanwhile, Union Minister HD Kumaraswamy launched a sharp attack on the Karnataka government, accusing it of failing to acknowledge corruption allegations despite officials allegedly being caught red-handed.

Kumaraswamy said that this "government is shameless in Karnataka. There are many officials being caught red-handed for involvement in corruption, and the chief minister. In today's conference, he says that there is no corruption in this government. This is the height of shamelessness of this government."

Earlier, Kumaraswamy also visited Cloudnine Hospital in Bengaluru's Jayanagar, where a one-and-a-half-year-old child is undergoing treatment after allegedly being administered a heavy dose of anaesthesia four months ago.

Expressing concern over the child's condition, the Union Minister blamed the hospital and its doctors for the child's suffering and alleged that the hospital management was now attempting to present different accounts of the incident.

He said that the alleged medical error had caused severe damage to the child's brain and that the parents were also not being treated properly by the hospital management.

"Because of the mistake of the hospital and the doctors, a one-and-a-half-year-old kid is suffering for no mistake from their parents. Now the hospital is trying to create different stories after the mistake which they made, which is causing huge damage to the brain of a small baby. Even parents are not being properly treated by the hospital management," he said.

Kumaraswamy said that he had instructed the hospital management to ensure that its authorised representatives meet him by 4 pm on Saturday to discuss the child's further treatment and provide clarifications.

"That is why I have instructed the official management of the hospital to bring their authorised people tomorrow by 4 o'clock to discuss further treatment. Parents have been very patient till now and the family and supporters are still maintaining peace. Even after facing so much trouble from the hospital, which is affecting their kid's life," he said.

He further warned that the child would be shifted to another hospital if the management failed to provide satisfactory answers and arrangements for further treatment.

"I have told the management clearly to bring their authorised people within 4 o'clock tomorrow to give proper treatment and further clarifications, or else we will shift the baby to a different place and we are capable of taking care of the baby. We will also ensure that a legal fight against the hospital will be conducted without any miss," Kumaraswamy said.

The Union Minister also said that the family and its supporters had so far maintained peace despite the difficulties faced during the child's treatment.

data.title: Green partnership gives India-Denmark ties distinct character: S Jaishankar
data.description:
External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar on Saturday said the Green Strategic Partnership (GSP) gives India-Denmark relations a distinctive character, bringing together Danish capabilities and India's scale and development priorities, as he held talks with Danish Foreign Minister Lars Løkke Rasmussen in New Delhi.

Highlighting the importance of the partnership, Jaishankar said the two countries had made progress in areas such as water, renewable energy, power and green shipping, while cooperation in health, food processing, agriculture and science and technology had further strengthened bilateral ties.

"Our Prime Ministers met this May on the margins of the third India-Nordic Summit, and today we have an opportunity to take stock of the progress in our ties, but also issues which were discussed between them. Among, in our agenda, of course, most important is our Green Strategic Partnership, which has given our relationship a very distinctive character. It brings together Danish capabilities and India's scale and development, and whether it's water, renewable energy, power, or green shipping, there is a lot that we are doing in the framework of the GSP," Jaishankar said.

 

He also welcomed Rasmussen's engagements with Indian companies working in emerging and frontier technologies, as well as defence and security, during his visit to Bengaluru.

Emphasising Denmark's role in India's development ambitions, Jaishankar said New Delhi viewed Copenhagen as an important partner in its goal of becoming a developed nation by 2047.

"What I do want to emphasize is, as we work towards a goal of Viksit Bharat, that is developed India by 2047, we do envisage Denmark as a very important partner in that effort. And that is reflected in the fact that we work with you on many of our national missions," he said.

Jaishankar also highlighted the contribution of Danish companies operating in India and welcomed a larger business presence and increased activities in both countries. He said the two governments could facilitate business by addressing issues and challenges faced by companies.

The External Affairs Minister said the two sides would discuss further prospects for cooperation in defence and security, emerging technologies, space, education, skills and mobility. He also called for greater engagement through existing joint working groups and expressed hope for a new joint action plan for 2026-31.

Jaishankar further underlined the importance of India-Denmark cooperation in the broader context of strengthening India-EU relations, appreciating Copenhagen's support for deepening the partnership and concluding the India-EU Free Trade Agreement.

Describing the current international environment as complicated and uncertain, he said the two sides would also exchange views on geopolitical and strategic developments.

Earlier, Rasmussen arrived in New Delhi on Saturday to co-chair the fifth India-Denmark Joint Commission Meeting with Jaishankar at Hyderabad House.

In a post on X, Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal welcomed the Danish Foreign Minister and said the meeting would focus on further strengthening the Green Strategic Partnership.

Rasmussen's November 27-28 visit includes engagements aimed at expanding bilateral cooperation in technology, innovation, space, quantum technology and defence.

On Friday, the Danish Foreign Minister visited Bengaluru, where he met representatives of Indian research, technology and industrial institutions, including the Centre for Cellular and Molecular Platforms (C-CAMP), quantum technology company QpiAI, the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) and Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL).

During his engagements, Rasmussen explored opportunities for collaboration in the space sector, including partnerships between Danish small and medium-sized enterprises and Indian space institutions. At HAL, he was briefed on the use of components supplied by Danish company HBK in India's Advanced Light Helicopter (ALH) Dhruv and Light Combat Helicopter, as well as in research and development testing of the Tejas fighter jet.

Rasmussen also met Karnataka IT Minister Priyank Kharge and representatives of Danish companies operating in the state to discuss Global Capability Centres and India's skilled technology workforce.

"You have an enormous talent pool with exactly the skills that Danish companies are looking for. We are not the only ones trying to attract Indian talent. So, we also want to make Denmark an attractive place for skilled Indian professionals to go for work," he said.

During the Bengaluru visit, Innovation Centre Denmark launched its report, 'Access to Tech Talent in India', examining opportunities for Denmark to recruit skilled Indian professionals amid growing demand for talent.

data.title: Groww's AI assistant can now place trades in more than 20 Indian languages
data.description:
Groww has expanded its in-house artificial intelligence (AI) investing assistant GR-1 to help users research stocks, understand company results and move from investment insights to buy or sell orders, subject to their explicit approval, in more than 20 Indian languages.
 
GR-1 was the highlight of Groww Next 2026, the investment platform's flagship technology event held in Bengaluru on Saturday, where it showcased a new range of AI-led products and investment features.
 
Other launches included family accounts, daily and weekly systematic investment plans (SIPs) starting at ₹100, minor accounts and an option allowing investors to sell bonds before maturity.
 
The company is positioning these offerings around the need to make investment research and financial guidance more accessible as India's retail investor base expands.
 

AI and the investment advice gap

India has around 1,000 Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi)-registered investment advisers, according to the regulator's chairman. It also has roughly one mutual fund distributor for every 4,000 Indians, according to an AMFI and Crisil study.
 
Groww believes AI could help bridge this gap by combining technology-led research with human oversight.
 
“AI brings the speed, our people bring the scrutiny, and the customer always makes the decision,” said Neeraj Singh, co-founder and chief technology officer of Groww.
 
GR-1 understands the screen a user is viewing, allowing it to provide contextual information without requiring the investor to repeatedly enter details.
 
The assistant operates on Groww's internal systems, which the company says allows tighter control over security and customer data.
 
Since the introduction of multilingual chat, around 15 per cent of daily queries have come in regional languages, the company said. Its speak-to-chat feature, being rolled out in phases, already accounts for nearly 20 per cent of daily queries, with a significant share coming from Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities.

MF Prime adds research-backed portfolio guidance

Groww is also expanding MF Prime, its opt-in mutual fund offering launched six months ago.
 
The service helps investors assess which mutual funds to buy, hold, rebalance or exit, addressing three common questions: where to invest, how a portfolio is performing and when to exit.
 
The platform combines AI-led analysis with checks by Groww's in-house research team before recommendations reach investors.

AI accelerates product development

The company said AI has also changed the pace at which it develops and launches products.
 
Around 70-80 per cent of the code behind its recently launched US stocks offering was written using AI, according to Groww.
 
Among the new features showcased at the event were minor accounts that parents or legal guardians can open and manage entirely online, and fully digital Hindu Undivided Family (HUF) accounts for families investing together.
 
The platform has also introduced daily and weekly SIP options starting at ₹100, aimed at gig workers, shopkeepers, freelancers and other investors who prefer smaller, more frequent investments rather than a single monthly instalment.
 
For active traders, its AI Insights feature identifies chart patterns as they emerge.
 
Groww has also begun rolling out a facility allowing customers to sell their bond holdings before maturity at prevailing market prices, expanding access to secondary-market liquidity.

From IPO investments to US stocks

Initial public offerings (IPOs) remain an important entry point for first-time investors on the platform.
 
Groww customers accounted for nearly 30 per cent of all IPO allocations in India in 2026 as of October, according to the company.
 
During the Jio Platforms IPO, around 36 lakh customers applied through Groww. For more than 2.5 lakh of them, it was their first investment in the financial markets, the company said.
 
Groww has also made US stocks available on its platform, allowing customers to access more than 10,000 US-listed stocks and exchange-traded funds (ETFs).
 
During the November correction in Nvidia, orders for the stock on Groww increased more than 15 times from the beginning of the month, the company said.
 
Ahead of Anthropic's Nasdaq listing on November 19, Groww introduced a pre-order facility for the stock. More than one lakh users showed interest on the product page within hours, according to the company.
 
Encouraged by the response, Groww plans to extend pre-order facilities to other prominent international listings.
 
“Our customers have grown up with us. The young professional who started a SIP with us years ago is now investing for a child, a family and the future,” said Lalit Keshre, co-founder and chief executive officer of Groww.
 
“Honestly, we feel we haven't covered even 1 per cent of our journey,” he added.

data.title: Growth to remain resilient in Q3FY27, inflation faces upside risks: FinMin
data.description:
While India's economic activity remains resilient, with momentum expected to sustain in the December quarter, weather-related uncertainties and demand during the wedding season could add to inflationary pressures in the near term, the finance ministry said on Saturday.
 
The retail inflation print for November is also expected to reflect the impact of an unfavourable base, the Monthly Economic Review (MER) for November mentioned. India’s Consumer Price Index (CPI) - which is used to measure retail inflation - for November last year was 104.01 as per the 2024 base year, but only 0.71 per cent as per the 2012 base year.
 
“Inflation may face near-term upside pressures from the persistence of (unfavorable) base effect and weather-related uncertainties, including the possibility of a strong El Nino,” the ministry said in its MER.
 
 
“With the festive season persisting into November and the onset of the wedding/nuptial season, upcoming inflation prints may face upside risks due to increased demand across food and non-food items,” it added.
 
The cautionary report comes after India's retail inflation in October rose to a two-year high of 6.09 per cent, breaching the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI's) tolerance band of 2-6 per cent.
 
However, a moderation in global crude oil prices, with benchmarks falling below $100 per barrel in early November, and a strengthening rupee following robust capital inflows could provide some relief from imported inflationary pressures, provided these trends persist, the review said.
 
Potential supply-side shocks arising from the West Asia conflict are likely to remain a key risk to wholesale and retail prices in India. Continued hostilities and risks to the Strait of Hormuz could also keep oil import bills and maritime freight rates volatile, the ministry said.
 
On the growth front, the ministry expects domestic economic activity to sustain its momentum in the December quarter, with high-frequency indicators pointing to continued expansion across goods movement, tax collections, energy consumption, and freight.
 
"Business activity is likely to remain firm, with new orders gaining pace and input cost pressures easing. Domestic demand should stay supportive, with sequential momentum in vehicle sales and continued strength in rural consumption," the review said.
 
Comfortable fertiliser availability bodes well for the rabi season, although sowing is at an early stage and reservoir storage remains below last year's level, it added.
 
India's gross domestic product (GDP) grew 7.8 per cent in the June quarter, while the October edition of the MER estimated growth at 7.35 per cent in the September quarter. The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) will release GDP estimates for the September quarter on November 30, 2026.
 
The external sector is also expected to remain resilient, supported by robust merchandise exports, a strong services trade surplus and adequate foreign exchange reserves, the ministry said.
 
"Nevertheless, the evolving geopolitical situation, alongside uncertainty surrounding global trade policies, could weigh on the outlook," it said, adding that resilient domestic fundamentals and adequate macroeconomic buffers would help the economy navigate emerging challenges.

data.title: Delhi HC bars Old Monk makers from bottling 'iQ' gin in similar packaging
data.description:
The Delhi High Court has restrained Old Monk makers from bottling its 'iQ' gin in a get-up which is deceptively similar to that of 'Greater Than' gin.

The high court clarified that Mohan Meakin Limited, which manufactures Old Monk and iQ gin, is not restrained from using the mark 'IQ' or its 'iQ' device for gin or for any other goods and added that the company was at liberty to sell its gin in a different get-up.

Justice Purushaindra Kumar Kaurav said plaintiff Nao Spirits And Beverages Private Limited, which manufactures and sells 'Greater Than' gin, has no monopoly over the colours black and white, and the defendant (Mohan Meakin) is free to use them in a manner which does not result in a get-up deceptively similar to that of the plaintiff.

 

"The new get-up must differ not merely in the shape of the bottle, but also in its dress, that is, the size and placement of the label, the colour arrangement, the placement of the device, and the typography and arrangement of the words on the label, so that the overall get-up, seen as a whole, is not deceptively similar to that of the plaintiff," the high court said while passing an interim order on November 26.

According to the plaintiff, Greater Than is its flagship product, and it is a London Dry Gin introduced in India in 2016 and one of the first homegrown craft gins in the Indian market.

The plaintiff's counsel said it is a case of passing off of the overall get-up of the plaintiff's gin, that is, the shape of its bottle together with its trade dress.

He contended that the defendant has copied the bottle along with the black-and-white scheme, the black cap, the placement of a large black angular device at the top centre of the label and the arrangement of 'LONDON DRY' in small letters over 'GIN' in large letters.

The defendant, which has been in the liquor trade for over 160 years, sells brands including Old Monk, Big Ben London gin and Jamun gin.

It submitted that it has been using the mark 'IQ' for beer since 1996 and launched gin under the impugned 'iQ' label in August 2023.

Its counsel submitted that there is no similarity between 'Greater Than' and 'iQ', and the plaintiff has no registration for its label or its bottle.

The counsel submitted that the bottle is an ordinary, generic and functional bottle and identical bottles are sold across the world and offered as stock designs by glass makers. In India, Haku vodka and Indri whisky use similar bottles, he added.

The court, however, said it was prima facie satisfied that the use of the impugned get-up by the defendant was likely to cause confusion and deception, including confusion as to affiliation, sponsorship or connection, among ordinary consumers as well as among the plaintiff's loyal consumers and the trade.

It said the plaintiff has made out a strong prima facie case of passing off in respect of the overall get-up of the defendant's iQ gin.

"The balance of convenience is also in favour of the plaintiff. The plaintiff has used its get-up since 2016 and has built its goodwill on it.

"The defendant entered the market with the impugned get-up only in August 2023. The defendant is an established company with several brands and a large turnover.

"The order proposed does not stop it from selling gin, or from using the mark 'IQ'; it only requires the defendant to sell its gin in a get-up of its own," the court said.

It further said that the inconvenience to the defendant of changing the dress of one product is far less than the harm to the plaintiff if the impugned get-up continues in the market during the pendency of the suit.

Public interest also lies in ensuring that consumers are not misled about the source of what they buy, the high court said.

It directed that till the disposal of the suit, the defendant is restrained from manufacturing, bottling, selling, offering for sale, distributing, displaying or otherwise dealing in gin in the existing get-up.

Considering that the products are liquor, sold through licensed channels under state excise regimes, the court said the defendant should file an affidavit within two weeks disclosing its stock of iQ gin in the existing get-up, at its premises, with its distributors or in transit.

The court asked the defendant not to manufacture or bottle any fresh stock of gin in this get-up and not to place any fresh order for these bottles.

It granted one month's time to the defendant to exhaust the existing stock after which the company should ensure that the product is removed from the shelves of the retail/wholesale outlets supplied by it or through its distributors.

The defendant should be free to re-bottle and re-label such stock in a get-up that complies with the directions, the court said.

data.title: Weather, supply risks may push up India inflation in coming months: FinMin
data.description:
Retail inflation is likely to edge higher in the coming months, driven by stronger demand for food and non-food items amid continuing festivities and the onset of the wedding season, a Finance Ministry report said on Saturday.

The Monthly Economic Review (MER) for November said the domestic economic activity is expected to sustain its momentum into the December quarter of the current fiscal year, with high-frequency indicators pointing to continued expansion across goods movement, tax collections, energy consumption and freight.

"Continued conflict in the Middle East, risks to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and global trade policy uncertainty remain the key factors in the outlook, but strong macroeconomic fundamentals and adequate buffers leave the economy well placed to navigate them," it said.

 

Continued Middle East unrest and Strait of Hormuz risks could keep oil import bills and maritime freight rates volatile. These supply-side shocks threaten to feed into broader wholesale and retail price indices in the coming months, the report said.

However, easing global crude oil prices, with benchmarks falling below $100 per barrel in early November alongside a firmer rupee backed by robust capital inflows, may provide some relief from imported inflationary pressures, provided the momentum lasts.

"With the festive season persisting into November and the onset of the wedding/nuptial season, upcoming inflation prints may face upside risks due to increased demand across food and non-food items," the MER said.

Retail inflation breached the Reserve Bank's inflation targeting ceiling for the first time in two years in October. The inflation print came in at 6.09 per cent, on a sharp spike in food inflation and an unfavourable base effect.

The MER said that the effect of an unfavourable/less- favourable base may extend into November inflation numbers as well.

"Inflation may face near-term upside pressures from the persistence of base effect and weather-related uncertainties, including the possibility of a strong El Nino.

"However, the recent moderation in crude oil prices below $100 per barrel and the strengthening of the rupee could help contain imported inflation, if sustained," it said.

On the manufacturing front, the report said that business activity is likely to remain firm, with new orders gaining pace and input cost pressures easing.

Domestic demand should stay supportive, with sequential momentum in vehicle sales and continued strength in rural consumption. Comfortable fertiliser availability bodes well for the rabi season, although sowing is at an early stage and reservoir storage is below last year's level.

"The economy enters the coming months with firm domestic momentum, with sustained consumption demand, a gradual broadening of private investment and continued policy support for manufacturing expected to underpin growth," the report noted.

The MER said that the external sector is expected to remain resilient, supported by robust merchandise exports, a strong services trade surplus and adequate foreign exchange reserves. Nevertheless, the evolving geopolitical situation, alongside uncertainty surrounding global trade policies, could weigh on the outlook.

"Notwithstanding these external uncertainties, resilient domestic fundamentals and adequate macroeconomic buffers provide the economy with the capacity to navigate emerging challenges," the MER added.

Foreign exchange reserves continued to provide an adequate external buffer, and at $705.3 billion as of November 13, 2026, the reserves are equivalent to 10 months of imports.

data.title: SC clears way for Hockey India elections on Dec 5, sets aside HC orders
data.description:
The Supreme Court on Saturday paved the way for Hockey India elections scheduled to be held on December 5 and set aside two orders of the Orissa High Court staying the poll process.

A bench of Justices K V Viswanathan and Arun Palli recalled the two show cause notices of Hockey India to Hockey Association of Odisha, which had proposed its reclassification from a permanent member to an associate member.

The bench said grievances of Hockey Odisha will be redressed by a committee headed by ex-apex court judge Justice A K Sikri.

It said the court cannot allow the prospect of players, who are performing so well and training hard on the ground, to be jeopardised, and allowed the election to Hockey India to be held on December 5.

 

On November 18, amid the ongoing internal strife within Hockey India, the Orissa High Court refused to vacate its interim stay on the election process of the governing body, observing that its bye-laws do not empower the secretary general to convene Executive Committee meetings without the orders of the president.

It had dismissed an interlocutory application seeking vacation of the interim stay order passed on November 6.

Hockey India had scheduled its elections for December 5, with the final electoral roll due on November 15 and the nomination process scheduled between November 22 and 24.

data.title: Mumbai leads with 43% data centre projects, Hyderabad 2nd: Knight Frank
data.description:
Mumbai accounts for the highest 43 per cent share in the total development pipeline of data centre projects across seven major cities, according to Knight Frank.

Real estate consultant Knight Frank India highlighted that the pipeline of data centre development currently accounts for 80 facilities across seven key markets.

These seven cities are -- Mumbai, Pune, Hyderabad, Bengaluru, Delhi-NCR, Chennai and Kolkata.

The consultant said the composition of the data centre facilities pipeline indicates a clear shift towards larger facilities.

Developments above 50 MW account for 55 per cent of the total pipeline in the July-September quarter of this year, reflecting an increased emphasis on larger-format infrastructure across India's key data centre markets.

 

"Mumbai continued to dominate India's data centre development pipeline, accounting for 34 of the 80 pipeline facilities in Q3 2026, or 42.5 per cent of the total," Knight Frank said.

Mumbai, the financial capital, recorded a 9.7 per cent increase from 31 facilities in 2025.

Out of 34 data centre projects in the pipeline in Mumbai, 18 facilities are in the above-50-MW segments.

Mumbai also remained the leading market for facilities above 100 MW, with their number increasing from 10 in 2025 to 15 in the September quarter of 2026.

The city additionally recorded 16 facilities in the 10-50-MW category, the highest among the seven markets, reinforcing its position across both mid-sized and large-format developments.

Hyderabad emerged as the second-largest contributor to the pipeline, with its total increasing from 11 facilities in 2025 to 15 in the September quarter.

The city's growth was led by the above-100-MW category, where the number of facilities doubled from four to eight.

Hyderabad also recorded six facilities in the 50-100-MW segment.

Consequently, 14 of its 15 pipeline facilities, or 93.3 per cent, fall within the above-50-MW categories, making Hyderabad the market with the highest concentration of larger-format developments.

This positions the city as an important emerging destination for large-scale data centre infrastructure, the consultant said.

data.title: Amit Shah urges all parties to support delimitation Bill, calls it historic
data.description:
Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Saturday said all parties should support the Constitution (132nd) Amendment Bill to effect a uniform 50 per cent rise in Lok Sabha seats across states and termed it a "historic initiative" to make women strong partners in governance.

In a message posted on X ahead of a special sitting of Parliament beginning next week, Shah said, "Giving women a stronger role in elected representation has been a commitment of the Modi government. With the Union Cabinet's approval of the 132nd Constitution Amendment Bill under Modi's leadership yesterday, the decades-long wait of the country's women is about to end." "The 33% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies, provided through the Nari Shakti Vandan Act, will now become a reality," he said.

 

"All parties should support this historic initiative to make women strong partners in governance," he added.

The government has convened a four-day special sitting of Parliament from November 30, during which it will bring three bills for the implementation of 33 per cent women's reservation in the Lok Sabha and state assemblies before the 2029 parliamentary elections, including the Constitution (132nd) Amendment Bill.

Shah said at least one-third representation for women in state assemblies will make the policies of states and Union territories more inclusive, while their presence in the Lok Sabha will add a new dimension to policymaking, lawmaking and the setting of national priorities.

"All parties should support this historic initiative to make women strong partners in governance," he said.

The Union Cabinet on Friday cleared the proposed Constitution amendment bill that seeks to increase the strength of the Lok Sabha from the present 543 seats to a maximum of 850 through delimitation.

The move will pave the way for the implementation of 33 per cent reservation for women in Parliament and state legislative assemblies ahead of the 2029 general elections.

A two-thirds majority in both Houses of Parliament is a must for a constitutional amendment bill to get cleared. The DMK, the NCP and the BRS, are expected to support the Bill.

The fresh bill seeks to use the 2011 Census to redraw the increased seats. There will be a freeze on seats till 2051.

The bill was brought in Parliament by the government during a special sitting in April, but it could not be passed as the ruling dispensation could not muster strength in the Lok Sabha.

The government has now claimed that it has the numbers to get the legislation through.
